title: Close the sign-up tickets left by the Java 21 move

blocks.text: The sign-up service was moved from Java 8 to Java 21, and its rules class was tidied on the way: the reserved user names became an unmodifiable set built once at startup. Since the release, three tickets are open:

items: a mobile client that leaves out the username field gets a 500 instead of the form's "username is required" message;
the nightly audit export sometimes lists a domain that was blocked after the export started;
monitoring raises "status page changed" after restarts in which no limit changed.

blocks.text: Finish the three `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/SignupRules.java`: `isReserved(...)`, `blockedDomains()` and `limitsReport(...)`. Each method's comment says what its caller needs. About five lines in total.

cases.says: a reserved user name is refused and any other name is accepted
the export gets every blocked domain, in the order they were blocked
the status report has one name=value line for each limit
a sign-up without a username is not reserved, and the check does not throw
a domain blocked after the export asked does not appear in what the export got
the report lists the limits ordered by name, whatever order the map iterates in

origin.section: List.of and Map.of Build Unmodifiable Collections That Reject null, Even in a Lookup

concepts: List.copyOf takes a snapshot; Collections.unmodifiableList is a view that shows later changes to the list behind it.
Collections from Set.of, List.of and Map.of throw NullPointerException on contains(null) or get(null), where HashSet answers false.
Map.of and Set.of iteration order is unspecified and changes between JVM starts.
